Subject: Hosted API latency commitments — questions and procurement timeline

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move through procurement, NovaHealth needs a clearer picture of the hosted API latency commitments (p50/p95) and how you measure them. Two things are important for our legal and SRE teams:

- Measurement windows: we have bursty, nightly batch traffic. If p95 is computed across a 30-day rolling window we could be unfairly penalized for occasional nightly peaks. Can you outline alternative windows (daily buckets, sliding windows, business-hours-only) you support?
- Exception policy: if a customer needs a different measurement approach, what operational and contractual guardrails (fallbacks, canary rollbacks, capacity reservations) do you require?

Procurement would like a proposed SLO matrix and any suggested contractual language by the end of next week. We can loop in legal if needed.

Thanks — I can be available for a short call Wednesday afternoon.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Reliability, NovaHealth

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@novahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments — questions and procurement timeline

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear bullets and for the timeline.

Short answers up front: we publish standard hosted API commitments and we can propose a limited exception for NovaHealth with explicit measurement windowing and an operational fallback plan.

What I propose before procurement drafts contract language:

1) Two SLO profile options (examples):
   - Standard: p50 = 60ms, p95 = 450ms (measured as a rolling 30-day window across all traffic)
   - Windowed: p50 = 60ms (all requests), p95 = 450ms (measured as daily 1-hour rolling buckets, aggregated to a 7-day rolling median) — this protects customers with short, high-volume bursts.

2) Exception guardrails: capacity reservation (soft reserve), automated fallback to a lightly quantized model variant during sustained congestion, and a canary rollback plan executed by our ops team.

I've sketched a tentative SLO matrix and a short exception draft (attached). Can we sync Thursday 10:00am PT to walk through? I'll also loop in Product (Marissa) and Runtime (Ben) so they can confirm feasibility.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SLO_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: NovaHealth SLO windowing — need ops/product sign-off

Marissa / Ben — forwarding inbound from NovaHealth. They asked for an alternate p95 measurement to avoid nightly-burst penalties.

Ask: can Product + Runtime approve a limited exception that includes:
- measurement approach: "daily 1-hour rolling buckets aggregated into a 7-day median" for p95 only (leave p50 global)
- operational controls: soft capacity reservation (up to 20% burst buffer), automatic fallback to quantized model variant when sustained p95 breaches > 5 mins, and playbook for canary rollback (who executes, SLAs on mitigation)
- telemetry requirements: NovaHealth must enable request-level tracing and share a sample prompt set during onboarding for our quality checks

I attached a quick draft of the contractual language and an SLO matrix. Please reply with any red flags or edits; procurement is on a tight timeline.

Thanks — Sean

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 13:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: NovaHealth SLO windowing — need ops/product sign-off

Thanks for the context. Quick notes from Product/Runtime:

- Feasibility: the proposed hybrid window is implementable. We measure p50 as a global percentile over all requests; for p95 we can support a "bucketed" measurement where we compute p95 across rolling 1-hour windows and then take a 7-day median of those daily p95s. This reduces sensitivity to multi-hour nightly spikes.

- Fallback: automatic fallback to a lower-precision model variant is acceptable, but we need acceptance criteria up-front: invocation threshold (e.g., sustained p95 > 700ms for 5 consecutive minutes) and a manual override for SREs. We'll add an automated alert to the NovaHealth project dashboard and require a signed playbook before go-live.

- Capacity reservation: soft reservation up to 20% is ok for a 6-month pilot (billing as usage but prioritized routing). If they commit to a 12-month reserved capacity contract we can discuss hard reservation.

I'll incorporate these into a short exception addendum and iterate with Legal. Ben, flag any infra risk.

— Marissa
Director, Product — Hosting & Runtime

Summary (what we can offer for NovaHealth pilot):
- p50: 60ms (global)

- Fallback: automatic model variant fallback when sustained p95>700ms for 5 consecutive minutes; automated alert to NovaHealth dashboard + manual override by Redwood SREs
- Capacity: soft reservation up to 20% for a 6-month pilot (billed as usage but prioritized routing)
